newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Habsburg denies smuggling diadem into Austria.
newsitem.headline: Habsburg denies smuggling diadem into Austria.

text.p: Karl Habsburg, grandson of the last Austro-Hungarian emperor, on Friday denied allegations he tried to smuggle a jewel-encrusted diadem into Austria to avoid paying import duty.

Habsburg, elected to the European Parliament last month to represent Austria's conservative People's Party, said in a statement he initially failed to mention the diadem to customs officials through an "error".
The incident happened at the end of June, when Austrian Foreign Minister and People's Party leader Wolfgang Schuessel had already named Habsburg as a top candidate in the European poll.
"I reject allegations of smuggling...I did not intend to import the diadem into Austria," Habsburg said in a statement, issued after Austrian radio broke news of the incident.
The 35-year old professional pilot and former games show host faces a hefty fine if found to have tried to flout regulations on importing valuable goods.
He explained that the diadem, borrowed from a Swiss foundation, was destined for Britain.

"My wife is permitted to borrow pieces from the foundation. In this case, she wanted to wear the jewellery at an event in England. It would then have been returned to Switzerland," the grandson of Emperor Karl I said.
Officers at Hohenems airfield in the western province of Vorarlberg, some 700 km (400 miles) west of Vienna, found the diadem during a search of a private plane used by Habsburg.
"On their second enquiry, I told them that the diadem was on board and agreed to a search," Habsburg said.
A customs official said any future fine would be based on the level of duty owed on the diadem. The burden of proof lies with Vorarlberg regional customs authority in Feldkirch.
Habsburg's office rejected media reports that have put the value of the diadem as high as 1.5 million schillings ($140,000).
"It is relatively valuable but certainly is not worth that much," a spokesman said.

Habsburg is one of six members of the European Parliament from the People's Party, which rules in coalition with the Social Democrats. In the legislature he has joined his father Otto, a German MEP for 17 years.
